payload.task_text:
I am a course administrator at Open University and I need to generate end-of-semester grade reports for all Spring 2014 courses. The Spring 2014 courses are identified by course codes containing "2014B".

There is a grading_policy.pdf file in the workspace that contains our official grading scale and special designation criteria. You must read this PDF first and apply its rules. The PDF specifies the following canonical thresholds that your output must follow exactly: letter grade A is awarded when the class average is 90.00 or above, B is 80.00 through 89.99, C is 70.00 through 79.99, D is 60.00 through 69.99, and F is below 60.00. The "With Distinction" designation is awarded when the class average is 85.00 or above. The "Academic Probation" flag is triggered when the class average falls below 50.00. All numeric values in the report (individual averages, summary averages) must be rounded to exactly 2 decimal places using standard mathematical rounding.

For each Spring 2014 course, look up the course in our learning management system and find the lead instructor. The lead instructor is the teacher enrolled in the course who comes first alphabetically by name. If a course has no teacher enrolled, use "N/A" for the instructor name and email, and skip sending an email for that course. Also find the number of students who have recorded scores (a non-null current_score in their enrollment grades) and calculate the class average score from those student scores.

Assign each course a letter grade based on its class average using the scale in the PDF. Also determine if the course qualifies for "With Distinction" honors or triggers an "Academic Probation" flag per the PDF criteria.

Create a file called semester_grade_report.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets.

The first sheet should be named "Course Grades" with the following columns: Course_Code, Course_Name, Lead_Instructor, Instructor_Email, Students_Scored, Class_Average (rounded to 2 decimal places), Letter_Grade, Distinction (write "Yes" or "No"), Probation (write "Yes" or "No"). Sort rows by Course_Code alphabetically. Course_Name should include the semester suffix in parentheses, e.g. "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)".

The second sheet should be named "Grade Distribution" with columns: Letter_Grade (list A, B, C, D, F in that order), Course_Count (how many courses received that letter grade), Courses (comma-separated course codes that received that grade, sorted alphabetically within each grade; leave empty string if no courses got that grade).

The third sheet should be named "Summary" with two columns (Metric, Value) containing the following rows: Total_Courses (the number of Spring 2014 courses), Avg_Class_Average (the average of all class averages rounded to 2 decimal places), Highest_Average_Course (the course code with the highest class average), Lowest_Average_Course (the course code with the lowest class average), Distinction_Count (how many courses earned the With Distinction designation), Probation_Count (how many courses are flagged for Academic Probation).

Also create a Google Sheet titled "Spring 2014 Grade Summary" with one sheet named "Grades" containing columns: Course_Code, Class_Average, Letter_Grade, Distinction, Probation for all six courses sorted by Course_Code.

Finally, send an email from registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk to each course's lead instructor (for courses that have a teacher) with the subject "End-of-Semester Grade Report: [Course Code]" where [Course Code] is replaced with the actual course code. The body should state the course name, the class average, the letter grade, and whether the course earned distinction or is on academic probation. Note: the registrar inbox and the cloud spreadsheet workspace may contain pre-existing unrelated messages and spreadsheets (such as IT maintenance notices, library notices, or historical registration reports). Do not forward, reference, or otherwise act on those unrelated items; only create the Spring 2014 grade report artifacts described above.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, dynamically collect every Spring 2014 score page, compute one canonical six-row payload, and make the workbook, Google Sheet, and instructor emails consume that payload verbatim. Do not embed expected course averages or instructor identities in the prompt.

The main agent resolves the accessible task workspace, reads grading_policy.pdf, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), and freezes the literal IDs/codes/full names of exactly the 2014B courses. For each retained course, call canvas_get_course_grades(page=1, per_page=1, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) in a native-parallel discovery batch; take pagination.total_count and derive the exact page set at per_page=100.

1. Wave 1 — after the student-page and teacher work items are frozen, dispatch exactly one explore sub-agent per item in one parallel response, never more than 128. Number student-page owners first, then teacher owners, N from 0:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Student-page owner for the first frozen `{course_id,course_code,course_name,page}`. Call canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=<ID></id>, page=<page></page>, per_page=100, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) exactly once and return only {course_id,course_code,page,pagination_page,pagination_total_count,returned_rows,scored_count,score_sum,score_min,score_max}, using enrollment.grades.current_score and ignoring nulls. Do not return enrollment rows.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Student-page owner for the second frozen page item — same literal recipe, only that page identity substituted.
      ...
      P. explore P-1 (enterprise-data-analyst P-1): Student-page owner for the last frozen page item — same literal recipe, only that page identity substituted.
      P+1. explore P (enterprise-data-analyst P): Teacher owner for the first Spring course. Call canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=<ID></id>, page=1, per_page=100, type=["TeacherEnrollment"]) and canvas_list_course_users(course_id=<ID></id>). Join teacher enrollment user_ids to users, sort matched teachers by complete name alphabetically, and return {course_id,course_code,teachers:[{user_id,name,email}],lead_instructor,lead_email,teacher_count,unmatched_teacher_ids}. If no teacher exists, return N/A for name/email. Do not modify Canvas.
      ...
      K. explore K-1 (enterprise-data-analyst K-1): Teacher owner for the last Spring course — same literal teacher recipe, only that course identity substituted. K = P + number of Spring courses.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies every discovered student page exactly once, summed returned_rows against total_count, and exactly one teacher result per course. Combine unrounded page sums, apply the policy and standard mathematical rounding once, and freeze one canonical six-row table:
{course_code,course_name,lead_instructor,instructor_email,students_scored,class_average_2dp,class_average_text_2dp,letter_grade,distinction,probation}.
Derive Grade Distribution and Summary from this table only. Assert every downstream class-average string is exactly class_average_text_2dp; no branch may re-query or recompute grades.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One Coder is the sole writer of semester_grade_report.xlsx in the dynamically resolved workspace. Create exactly Course Grades, Grade Distribution, and Summary with the exact headers/order and literal canonical values, then read all populated ranges back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): One Coder is the sole owner of the Google spreadsheet titled Spring 2014 Grade Summary. Create it once, create/use only sheet Grades, write precisely the header and six canonical rows to A1:E7, and read A1:E7 back. Do not add diagnostic cells.

In the same response that launches Wave 2, the main agent searches Sent mail in native parallel for every canonical row whose instructor email is not N/A, matching complete From registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk, To, and subject End-of-Semester Grade Report: <Course Code></course>. Send only missing messages. Each body must copy the literal canonical course_name, class_average_text_2dp, letter_grade, distinction, and probation fields without recalculation. Read every retained email back.

After Wave 2, reconcile workbook, sheet and emails against the identical canonical rows and exact two-decimal strings. Do not dispatch a verification wave.

You are gathering grade data from Canvas LMS for Open University's Spring 2014 courses.

**Task**: For each of the 6 Spring 2014 courses listed below, retrieve all student enrollment grades via the Canvas MCP tools, calculate the class average from students with a non-null `current_score`, and return the results as a JSON summary.

**The 6 Spring 2014 courses** (identified by course code containing "2014B"):
1. Course id=6 (course_code "BBB-2014B"): Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)
2. Course id=8 (course_code "CCC-2014B"): Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)
3. Course id=12 (course_code "DDD-2014B"): Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)
4. Course id=15 (course_code "EEE-2014B"): Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014)
5. Course id=19 (course_code "FFF-2014B"): Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014)
6. Course id=22 (course_code "GGG-2014B"): Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014)

**For each course, do the following**:

1. Use `mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades` with:
   - `course_id`: the course id
   - `type`: `["StudentEnrollment"]`
   - `per_page`: 100
   - `page`: 1, then iterate `page=2`, `page=3`, ... until `pagination.has_more` is false
2. For each enrollment object, if `grades.current_score` is non-null, collect the score.
3. After iterating through all pages, compute:
   - `students_scored`: count of students with non-null `current_score`
   - `class_average`: arithmetic mean of all those scores (keep full precision; do not round yet)

**Final deliverable**: Print a JSON object to stdout with this exact shape (no comments, valid JSON):

```json
{
  "BBB-2014B": {"course_id": 6, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "CCC-2014B": {"course_id": 8, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "DDD-2014B": {"course_id": 12, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "EEE-2014B": {"course_id": 15, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "FFF-2014B": {"course_id": 19, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "GGG-2014B": {"course_id": 22, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>}
}
```

**Important**:
- The page counts can be up to ~17 per course (since each course has ~1500-2400 students). Be patient and paginate fully.
- Do not round or truncate the class_average — return the full-precision float (we'll round to 2 decimals later).
- If a student has `grades: {}` (empty), skip that student entirely (no current_score).
- Only use non-null `current_score` values. Do not use `final_score` instead — the task specifies `current_score`.
- Return ONLY the JSON in your final answer. Do not include any commentary before or after.

Begin.
Gather student grades for Spring 2014 courses

You are gathering Canvas LMS grade data for 6 Spring 2014 courses and computing class averages.

**Task**: For each of the 6 Spring 2014 courses, paginate through student enrollments, extract `current_score` values, and compute the class average. Save raw data to files in the workspace and emit a JSON summary.

**The 6 Spring 2014 courses** (course code contains "2014B"):
- Course id=6 (BBB-2014B): Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)
- Course id=8 (CCC-2014B): Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)
- Course id=12 (DDD-2014B): Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)
- Course id=15 (EEE-2014B): Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014)
- Course id=19 (FFF-2014B): Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014)
- Course id=22 (GGG-2014B): Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014)

**Step-by-step procedure**:

1. For each course, use `mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades` with `course_id`, `per_page=100`, `page=N`, and `type=["StudentEnrollment"]` to fetch each page.
2. **IMPORTANT**: For each page response, immediately call `mcp__filesystem__write_file` to save the entire JSON response to a file (path like `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-pdf-grade-gsheet/workspace/.canvas_cache/course_<id>_page_<N>.json`). Do NOT try to parse or summarize in your context — just write the raw response to disk.
3. After writing the file, capture the `pagination.has_more` value and `pagination.total_pages` from the response to decide whether to fetch more pages. Iterate `page=1, 2, ..., total_pages`.
4. Make the canvas API calls in parallel batches (you can fire many at once in a single response). Then immediately write each response to a file.

**After all pages are saved to disk**:

5. Use `mcp__local__python_execute` to read each JSON file and aggregate: for each course, sum all non-null `current_score` values from the `grades` object across all student enrollments, count how many students had a non-null score, then compute the class average.
6. Use Python's `json` and `glob` libraries to do this efficiently. Save the aggregated result to `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-pdf-grade-gsheet/workspace/.canvas_cache/averages.json`.

**Filter rules**:
- Skip any enrollment where `grades == {}` or `grades` is missing.
- Use `current_score` (a number) — NOT `final_score`, NOT `current_grade` (which is a string like "Distinction"/"Pass"/"Merit"/"Fail").
- A `current_score` of 0.0 counts as a valid scored student. Only skip when the field is absent/null.

**Step 1 — first batch of fetches and writes** (fire all in parallel in one response):
- course_id=6, page=1 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_6_page_1.json`
- course_id=6, page=2 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_6_page_2.json`
- course_id=8, page=1 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_8_page_1.json`
- course_id=8, page=2 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_8_page_2.json`
- course_id=12, page=1 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_12_page_1.json`
- course_id=15, page=1 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_15_page_1.json`
- course_id=19, page=1 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_19_page_1.json`
- course_id=22, page=1 → write to `.canvas_cache/course_22_page_1.json`

(That's 8 parallel calls per batch. Aim for ~6-8 canvas calls per batch so you can write each response to a file in the same response. Don't make MORE than ~10 canvas calls per response — keep it manageable.)

After each canvas response, immediately write that response to the matching file path.

**Pagination**: After writing page 1 of a course, you will see `pagination.total_pages` (e.g. 17 for course 6). Make subsequent batches for pages 2..total_pages for that course.

**Final deliverable**: Once you have all pages cached and the Python aggregation done, emit a JSON object EXACTLY in this shape (no commentary, valid JSON only):

```json
{
  "BBB-2014B": {"course_id": 6, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "CCC-2014B": {"course_id": 8, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "DDD-2014B": {"course_id": 12, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "EEE-2014B": {"course_id": 15, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "FFF-2014B": {"course_id": 19, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>},
  "GGG-2014B": {"course_id": 22, "students_scored": <int>, "class_average": <float>}
}
```

**Final deliverable format**: Print ONLY the JSON object (plus a brief one-line note about file locations) at the very end of your final reply. Do not pad with prose. Do not claim task completion — return findings to the parent.

Gather and aggregate Spring 2014 grades

You are collecting course grade data from Canvas LMS via the `mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades` tool. For each of 6 courses, fetch all pages and write compact per-page score files to disk.

## Target courses (course_id and total_pages for each):
- Course 6 (BBB-2014B): 17 pages
- Course 8 (CCC-2014B): 20 pages  
- Course 12 (DDD-2014B): 13 pages
- Course 15 (EEE-2014B): 7 pages
- Course 19 (FFF-2014B): 15 pages
- Course 22 (GGG-2014B): 9 pages
- Total: 81 pages

## What to do for each course, for each page:
1. Call `mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades` with `course_id=<cid>`, `page=<n>`, `per_page=100`. (No need to filter by type — just fetch all.)
2. From the returned JSON, extract only the StudentEnrollment entries that have a non-null `current_score` (under `enrollment.grades.current_score`).
3. Build a compact array: `[{user_id, current_score}, ...]`
4. Write to `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-pdf-grade-gsheet/workspace/.canvas_cache/course_<cid>_page_<n>_scores.json` as JSON of the form `{"course_id": <cid>, "page": <n>, "count": <k>, "scores": [...]}`. Use the `mcp__filesystem__write_file` tool.

## Strategy to avoid context overflow
- Process ONE PAGE at a time.
- After each fetch+write, immediately move on to the next page. Do NOT keep raw responses in your context.
- After writing the scores JSON for that page, you may mentally forget the full payload.
- The full course_grades response is discarded after you extract scores; only the compact scores JSON goes to disk.

## Order
Process in this order so partial progress is recoverable:
1. Course 6 pages 1-17
2. Course 8 pages 1-20
3. Course 12 pages 1-13
4. Course 15 pages 1-7
5. Course 19 pages 1-15
6. Course 22 pages 1-9

You can fetch up to 3 pages in parallel per response (they're independent). Then write all 3 score files in the next response. Or do them one at a time if you prefer.

## Final report
After all pages are written, return a brief summary listing how many score files you wrote and any pages you could not fetch. Also confirm the workspace directory has the files.

You do NOT need to aggregate, compute averages, or read existing files. ONLY fetch + extract + write per-page score files. The parent agent will aggregate.

Available tools include:
- `mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades` (course_id, page, per_page)
- `mcp__filesystem__write_file`, `mcp__filesystem__list_directory`, `mcp__filesystem__read_file`
- `mcp__local__python_execute` (if useful)
